correctness.rationale: The forward residue-class argument proves nonsynchronization when gcd(n,h)>1. For gcd=1 the complete interval-preimage analysis shows every reset word must contain n−1 growth steps and at least n−h inverse rotations between each consecutive pair. The explicit word attains that lower bound for every n≥2. Independent forward BFS checks every one of the 66 automata n=2..12; all match the closed formula, including nonsynchronizing cases; inverse intervals and witnesses were also replayed directly.

evidence: Volkov (2024) Corollaries 2.4–2.5 (doi:10.1051/ita/2024003) guarantee synchronization under primitivity and defect-one hypotheses, not shortest lengths.

Rystsov (2025), Thms 4.4 and 4.5, gives a general quadratic upper bound and a characterization of when the generated monoid is synchronizing, but no parameterwise exact minimum for a fixed forward generator.
Don (2016), §4 Proposition 15, gives (n−1)^2 upper bound and gcd sufficient condition.
broader_coverage.reasoning: General results prove connectivity/synchronization and upper bounds; they do not imply exact optimality. A general quadratic bound is strictly weaker than 1+(n-2)(n-h+1) for h>1.

equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The claim is about the shortest length with only a forward +1 generator, not just the existence of a reset word. The inverse-interval lower bound rules out all shorter words.

originality.rationale: The exact all-word lower bound via cyclic inverse intervals is not contained in the inspected coverage. Don (2016) Proposition 15 proves synchronization and the classical (n−1)^2 upper bound for coprime distance; Rystsov (2025) Theorems 4.4–4.5 cover the gcd synchronization criterion and give a word that specializes to our matching upper-bound witness. Those pieces are explicitly credited. Neither gives a lower bound requiring (n-2)(n-h) rotations between growing inverse images. This exact parameterwise minimum remains non-implied by the inspected published statements. Separate textual and mathematical-record queries found no stronger exact coverage, subject to specific residual literature risk.
residual_risks: An equivalent exact lower-bound calculation may exist in older unindexed work on cyclic generators and simple idempotents, particularly Rystsov (2000) and (2022), whose primary full texts were not completely retrieved.
No negative novelty claim is made about unread full documents or unpublished material. The previously known gcd criterion and upper-word construction are expressly credited.

The author transcription of the 2025 preprint has garbled some mathematical glyphs; the relevant theorem statements and construction were legible, but a detailed native PDF comparison could expose more overlap.

value.rationale: Shortest reset-word length is a central exact invariant in synchronizing automata. This theorem classifies an entire natural two-letter family with a single rank-(n−1) merge and a directed cycle. It determines all parameterwise shortest lengths from the classical quadratic extremum to linear behavior, a conclusion not furnished by known existence or upper-bound theorems. The inverse-interval lower-bound invariant is substantive and can guide other oriented-unitary automaton analyses; the claim is not just a known Černý substitution.
